Web research (read-only; no installs; no files except your answer). Date-stamp 2026-10-11. Context: scoup.ai (freight cost recovery for US trucking; founder Norwegian) wants to predict time-varying freight costs for customers (truckload spot/contract rates, fuel surcharges, reefer rates, ocean container rates) and must BACKTEST any prediction on real data. Find:
1. FREE downloadable real price time series with direct URLs that work without login (verify with WebFetch/curl-like checks), licence, frequency, history length: FRED series IDs (diesel weekly GASDESW, PPI truckload PCU4841214841212 and related, deep sea freight PPI, Cass indexes if any on FRED, import price indexes), EIA weekly on-highway diesel by PADD, USDA AMS Agricultural Refrigerated Truck Quarterly and the weekly "Specialty Crops Truck Rate Report"/National Truck Rate data (lane-level real truck rates — find CSV/API endpoints, e.g. MyMarketNews API), USDA Grain Transportation Report datasets (truck/barge/ocean rates), BTS Transportation Services Index, Freightos FBX/Drewry WCI public history, Cass Freight Index linehaul (public PDFs?), DAT public trendlines (national averages by month).
2. Industry leaders in freight rate prediction/benchmarking and their claimed accuracy and pricing: DAT iQ / RateView forecasts, SONAR (FreightWaves) TRAC/forecasts, Greenscreens.ai, Uber Freight, Loadsmart, Xeneta (ocean), Freightos. Note any published backtest/accuracy figures and how measured; grade vendor claims C.
3. Academic evidence on truckload rate / diesel price forecastability vs naive random-walk (papers, e.g. on spot rate cycles, MIT CTL work by Caplice, Acocella et al.), so we know realistic targets.
4. How fuel surcharges are computed (DOE/EIA weekly diesel, base price, cents-per-mile step tables, e.g. typical $1.20 base, $0.01/mile per $0.06) with public carrier FSC tables (URLs).
Return a compact report (~1200 words, tables, URL + grade), with the 8 most useful series for a backtest and exact download URLs.

## Freight price data and forecasting benchmarks (research as of 2026-10-11)

Grades: **A** means I downloaded it myself with no login (curl, 2026-10-11) and checked the header and last date. **B** means an official or peer-reviewed page I read but did not download as data. **C** means a vendor's own claim, not checked by anyone independent.

KMA forecasts come from an AI time-series model (https://sonar.freightwaves.com/?p=10218) | No error figures. User reviews say "mixed results" on accuracy (Capterra) |

I found no vendor that publishes accuracy against a random-walk baseline over a stated horizon on held-out data.

### 3. Academic evidence: realistic targets

- **Rana & Caplice, "Forecasting Long Haul Truckload Spot Market Rates", MIT CTL 2020** (https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/124451). Weekly US spot rates at 1, 4, 8 and 12-week horizons, measured by MAPE. A naive (random-walk) forecast **beat** ARIMA, other autoregressive models and elastic-net regression on economic indicators **at every horizon**. Rana's 2019 thesis (https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/123236) tested Naive, moving average, ARIMA and neural networks at regional level. The abstracts give no MAPE numbers. Grade B.
- **Roman & Kirirak capstone** (supervised by Caplice and Acocella). A VAR model of spot and contract rates, framed around the market cycle (https://scm.mit.edu/news-and-events/reading-the-freight-forecast-making-sense-of-the-truckload-market-cycle). Grade B.
- **Acocella, Caplice & Sheffi, "Elephants or Goldfish?"** (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2108.07348). Carriers' acceptance of contract tenders depends on current market conditions and current price. They do not remember how shippers behaved in earlier periods. So the gap between contract and spot rates, not history, drives contract leakage. Grade B.
- **Budak, Ustundag et al., "A forecasting approach for truckload spot market pricing"** (https://research.itu.edu.tr/en/publications/a-forecasting-approach-for-truckload-spot-market-pricing/). An ML model at lane level. I did not check its error figures.
- **Diesel / energy.** EIA's NEMS model beat a random walk at the one-year horizon (26% lower MAPE). At other horizons it was mixed, and simple models matched it (https://ageconsearch.umn.edu/record/208082). EIA's STEO missed March 2011 diesel by $0.53/gal (https://www.ccjdigital.com/business/article/14924817/forecasting-diesel-prices-provided-they-dont-change). Grade B.

**Implications:**
- Use random walk as the required baseline. Report each model's MAPE as a ratio to it (Theil's U), at 1, 4, 13 and 52 weeks.
- For spot TL, matching or slightly beating no-change is a realistic result.
- Fuel surcharge (FSC) is different. It is close to mechanically predictable one week ahead, because retail diesel lags wholesale. That last point is my general knowledge, not something I checked here.

### 4. How fuel surcharges are computed

- **Index:** EIA's US national average on-highway diesel, posted Monday (Tuesday after holidays). It usually applies to shipments from the following Wednesday through Tuesday. GSA's federal FSC rule says exactly this. It is percentage-based, with baselines set in Nov 2000 (https://origin-www.gsa.gov/system/files/Fuel%20Surcharge%20%28effective%2010-1-21%29.pdf). Grade B (I read the PDF text).
- **Per-mile formula:** FSC = (DOE price − base) ÷ MPG. A $1.20 base at 6 MPG works out to +$0.01/mile per $0.06 of diesel.
- **Bison Transport USA table** (https://www.bisontransport.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/10/Fuel-Surcharge-Bison-USA.pdf), read from the PDF text. Starts at $0.01/mile at $1.12–1.16, then **+1¢/mile per 5¢ step**, which implies about 5 MPG. For example, $3.57–3.61 gives $0.50 and $5.72–5.76 gives $0.93. Grade B.
- **States Logistics LTL/drayage table** (https://stateslogistics.[REDACTED:high_entropy].pdf). Percentage steps per 1¢: $1.20–1.25 gives 2.52%, $2.00–2.01 gives 12.06%. Grade B.
- **Carrier bases quoted by a third party** (https://www.oilpriceapi.com/fuel-surcharge): J.B. Hunt $1.20/6 MPG, Schneider $1.15/6, Werner $1.22/6. Grade C; I did not check these against the carriers' own documents.
- **Backtest note:** every shipper-specific FSC table can be rebuilt exactly from GASDESW plus that shipper's base, step and MPG. A billed FSC that differs from the recomputed one is a recoverable overcharge. This needs only public data.

### 5. The 8 most useful series for a backtest

1. GASDESW, US diesel, weekly 1994 to: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=GASDESW
2. EIA diesel by PADD, weekly: https://agtransport.usda.gov/api/views/x88w-atzp/rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD
3. USDA reefer lane rates, weekly 2000 to, 206,785 lane-weeks. This is the only free lane-level real truck rate data I found: https://agtransport.usda.gov/api/views/acar-e3r8/rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD
4. USDA reefer weighted US $/mile, quarterly: https://agtransport.usda.gov/api/views/8xc6-nwjr/rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD
5. PPI long-distance TL, monthly 1992 to. It mixes contract and spot and is a price index, not $/mile: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=PCU4841214841212
6. PPI deep-sea freight, monthly 1988 to: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=PCU4831114831115
7. Cass Freight Index Expenditures, monthly 2016 to (cite Cass): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=FRGEXPUSM649NCIS
8. Drewry container spot sample, monthly 2012 to. Westbound US→Shanghai only, so it does not stand in for import rates: https://agtransport.usda.gov/api/views/dtp5-fwp8/rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD

Useful covariates: TSIFRGHT (fredgraph.csv?id=TSIFRGHT) and the USDA grain cost index (8uye-ieij).

**Gaps:**
- There is no free long history of dry-van spot or contract rates in $/mile. DAT, SONAR and Cass linehaul are licensed or chart-only.
- The diesel series reads $6.199/gal for 2026-10-05. That is unusually high, and FRED and USDA agree on it. Sanity-check it before using it in any claim.
- Per the project's honesty rule, no accuracy figure should be quoted in product or marketing material until our own walk-forward backtest against random walk exists.

No files were written; the scratchpad holds only a cached JSON list of datasets.
